description: Shared correctness fixtures (docs/benchmark-correctness-fixtures.md). One xorshift64 stream (seed=42, n=1000000) drives three datasets (byteFlags, intThresholds, mixedHotCold) and four arrangement/implementation variants (biased9010, random5050, sorted, branchless). Both languages must reproduce every value below exactly: sequences via identical unsigned 64-bit integer arithmetic (Java: java.lang.Long unsigned operators; Rust: native u64), filtered sums via identical wrapping accumulation. The sorted and branchless variants apply to the SAME underlying random5050 data (permutation and implementation-technique changes only) so their filteredSum MUST equal random5050's filteredSum bit-for-bit — this equality is itself a correctness oracle, not just a fixture to reproduce. Change a value here only together with both test files.

semantics.xorshift64: x ^= x << 13; x ^= x >>> 7 (unsigned/logical); x ^= x << 17 (64-bit wrapping, unsigned interpretation throughout)
semantics.streamValue: s = the raw xorshift64 output at each step, interpreted as UNSIGNED 64-bit for all modulo operations
semantics.biasArrangement: isAbove = (s unsigned-mod 100) < biasPercent; biasPercent=90 for biased9010, biasPercent=50 for random5050 and (pre-sort) sorted and (pre-technique-change) branchless

mixedHotCold.note: kind and payload are both derived from the SAME stream value s at each index — not two independent streams

semantics.sortedTransform: ascending sort of the random5050 value array (byteFlags/intThresholds); for mixedHotCold, a STABLE sort of (kind,payload) pairs by kind ascending (cold block then hot block, payload order preserved within each block)
semantics.branchlessTransform: same random5050 data and predicate as the random5050 variant; only the accumulation technique changes (arithmetic mask/multiply instead of an if-branch) — not a new dataset
semantics.filteredSum: wrapping 64-bit sum of value (or payload) over every element where the predicate is true; setup/generation/sorting excluded from the timed region
semantics.checksum: checksum*31 + value, 64-bit wrapping, over the full sequence (values as generated, pre-sort)

operationDefinition: one benchmark operation = one full pass over the declared dataset's 1,000,000 elements, accumulating the wrapping filtered sum via either the branchy (if-statement) or branchless (arithmetic mask) technique per the variant; the returned sum is consumed (used as the benchmark result) to block dead-code elimination

branchless.note: operates on IDENTICAL data to random5050 (no separate generation) — filteredSum for every dataset MUST equal the random5050 filteredSum above; this is asserted directly, not restated as separate numbers
